newsitem.title: UK: Halifax rate hike won't halt housing upturn.
newsitem.headline: Halifax rate hike won't halt housing upturn.

text.p: Britain's biggest home loan provider Halifax Building Society said on Tuesday its mortgage rate increase would not halt the recovery in the country's housing market.

Chief executive Mike Blackburn said in a statement, "Mortgage rates are still at a relatively low level and it is clear that the housing market is continuing to recover. We do not believe this increase will halt the recovery."
Halifax earlier said it was raising its UK mortgage rates to 7.6 percent from 7.25 percent, effective immediately for new borrowers and from June 1 for existing borrowers.
The rise follows a hike in UK base rates to 6.25 percent from 6.0 percent, ordered by Britain's new Labour government, which won a landslide victory at last week's general election.
Other mortgage lenders said they were keeping their rates under review after the base rate increase.

Northern Rock Building Society said it was monitoring the situation, saying the rise obviously put pressure on mortgage rates. Woolwich Building Society also said it was keeping its rates under review.
